verdict: DEF-001 accepted against every machine-verifiable criterion. CERTIFY-001 remains self-reviewed, and the residual risk of a self-review is stated below rather than papered over.

theInnoDesign.whyNotJustClamp: Clamping the balance alone breaks the books: the movement still records 999 while the balance shows 0, so every report that re-derives the balance from the movements disagrees with the item page. A number that looks right and books that do not balance is worse than a negative number.
theInnoDesign.consequence: Incoming stock settles debt before it becomes spendable, so a receipt cannot quietly turn an unfulfilled issue into phantom stock.

verification.unit: 14/14, including a deterministic randomised property test over 600 sequences x 25 steps x 3 policies asserting the invariant after every movement
verification.adversarialProbes: 11/11 with zero findings (was 10/11 with one finding before the fix)
verification.fullRegression: 43/43 E2E across every suite in the repository

findingsRaisedByThisReview.title: The deficit queue was reachable by an anonymous caller
findingsRaisedByThisReview.detail: The new controller was missing @UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard, RbacGuard), so GET /api/stock-deficits answered 200 to an unauthenticated request and disclosed every item name and shortfall. A contract test asserts the guard is present.
findingsRaisedByThisReview.foundBy: the E2E case that checks the queue is private, which failed with 200 instead of 401

findingsRaisedByThisReview.title: A partial settlement rounded a debt to zero
findingsRaisedByThisReview.detail: The first implementation closed the whole deficit row on a partial payment, so paying 300 of 989 silently erased the remaining 689. The remainder now opens a fresh record and stays visible.
findingsRaisedByThisReview.foundBy: reading the settle loop rather than the happy path, then driving it with a partial payment

findingsRaisedByThisReview.title: A concurrent write conflict was reported as a 500
findingsRaisedByThisReview.detail: Two over-issues for the same item collide under serialisable isolation. Prisma reports P2034, but the Postgres driver adapter wraps it in a DriverAdapterError, so the existing `error.code === 'P2034'` check never matched and the conflict escaped as a server fault. isWriteConflict now inspects the nested cause, and a surviving conflict becomes a retryable 409.
findingsRaisedByThisReview.foundBy: an adversarial probe that issued two over-issues at the same instant and looked at the status codes

findingsRaisedByThisReview.title: Writing a deficit off left the ledger unreconciled
findingsRaisedByThisReview.detail: Closing a deficit only relabelled the row, which broke currentStock === ledgerNet + openDeficit and turned the reconciliation permanently red. A write-off now also records an auditable correction movement that offsets the phantom demand, without touching the balance column because no goods arrived.
findingsRaisedByThisReview.foundBy: stock-adjustment.spec.ts failing on consistent === false, then reading the mismatch rows

findingsRaisedByThisReview.title: The per-item deficit totals ignored the item filter
findingsRaisedByThisReview.detail: The aggregate for openCount/openQuantity queried every open deficit regardless of the requested item, so one item's page reported another item's debt.
findingsRaisedByThisReview.foundBy: the E2E case that reads a single item's deficit and got 2667 for an item that owed 989

method: Black-box property attacks against the six declared behaviours, deliberately not a re-read of the code: simulated hostile sequences, concurrent requests, and checks that the books reconcile after every state. The build was verified by executing it, not by inspecting it.
residualRiskOfSelfReview: I wrote the design, the tests and this review, so a blind spot in my understanding of the warehouse domain would be invisible in all three. Specifically: whether an over-issue should clamp at all, or whether a pick should be blocked at the point of issue, is a business decision I inferred rather than one I was told.
The property test explores the arithmetic exhaustively but the sequence generator is mine, so it cannot prove the absence of a state I never imagined.
No human has read this code. A reviewer with fresh eyes would be the thing most likely to find a requirement I silently reinterpreted.
Concurrency was probed for two simultaneous issues on one item. Wider contention, and the interaction with the offline replay path, were not probed.
notProven: The Service Worker's own fetch cannot be cut by setOfflineMode, CDP emulation or request interception, so a genuine mid-request network interruption in the browser is still unproven; the durable queue is proven by offline-queue.spec.ts.

docker compose build (default target) still fails in this environment because the Puppeteer Chrome download is blocked. All verification used --target production, which is the same application code without the browser tooling.
